hook: The preacher who led the civil rights movement with nonviolence, and had a dream.

pages.x: Martin Luther King Jr. was born in Atlanta in 1929, the son and grandson of Baptist preachers. As a small boy he was told by a white friend's parents that the two could no longer play together. He started college at 15.

In 1955, aged 26 and the new pastor of a church in Montgomery, he was chosen to lead the bus boycott after Rosa Parks was arrested. His house was bombed, but he told his angry supporters not to answer violence with violence.
Jailed during protests in Birmingham in 1963, he wrote a long letter in the margins of a newspaper, arguing that people have a moral duty to disobey unjust laws, and that justice could not wait.

On 28 August 1963, before some 250,000 people at the March on Washington, he spoke of his dream of an America where his four children would be judged by who they were, not by the colour of their skin.
pages.img: March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom

pages.x: In 1964, at 35, he became the youngest winner of the Nobel Peace Prize up to that time, and gave the prize money to the movement.
The movement won the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which banned segregation, and the Voting Rights Act of 1965, after marchers from Selma were beaten by police on a bridge.
He turned to fighting poverty and spoke out against the Vietnam War, which cost him some allies. The FBI spied on him for years, and once sent him an anonymous threatening letter.

In April 1968 he went to Memphis to support striking rubbish collectors. In his last speech he said he had seen the promised land, though he might not get there with them. The next evening he was shot dead on his motel balcony. He was 39.
King led the civil rights movement with nonviolence and helped end legal segregation in America. A national holiday in January honours him.
